subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class browser-plugin contract for per-profile proxy settings plus per-agent/subagent browser-profile binding, or keep this as external orchestration through remote CDP, multiple Gateways, node-host profiles, or ClawHub packages?
rationale: The missing capability is source-confirmed, but implementing it defines public config, proxy credential handling, browser egress policy, logged-in session ownership, and subagent inheritance semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design core browser contract
options.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, SSRF trust, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella while #60035 owns broader proxy policy and #85672 owns subagent attachment and operator visibility semantics.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document remote CDP, multiple Gateways, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub packages as the supported path if maintainers do not want core config.

recommendation.title: Design core browser contract
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, SSRF trust, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across browser profile config, browser plugin ownership, docs, and security-sensitive browser control paths.
